newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to seek $610 mln loan from Japan.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to seek $610 mln loan from Japan.

text.p: Bangladesh will seek $610 million in fresh development loans from Japan during talks between the two countries beginning in Dhaka on Wednesday, government officials said on Tuesday.
They said the government would request soft loans for eight projects, involving mainly infrastructure, electricity and port development.
An eight-member Japanese mission, led by a senior foreign ministry official, is already in Dhaka for the first such talks in two years.
Tokyo denied Dhaka fresh aid for those two years, having expressed dissatisfaction with the way past aid had been used.

Japan had been one of the largest bilateral donors to Bangladesh, offering on an average $200 million annually. The lion's share came in the form of soft loans from the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund.

"The mission (from Japan) is very important. It indicates that the new Bangladesh government of Sheikh Hasina has earned the confidence of the Japanese government ... Japanese aid is very important to us," a Bangladesh finance ministry official told Reuters.
A senior Japanese diplomat in Dhaka told reporters recently that Japan was happy with the changes the present government had made in its decision-making.
"Now, suddenly it's a big change in a good direction," said Shuhei Takahashi of the Japanese embassy in Dhaka.
But government officials said the Japanese mission had asked for a comprehensive briefing on the economic policies of the Hasina government, which took office last June.
